description.narrative: **Improving health outcomes and poverty indicators requires an inclusive approach to sanitation and health.** An approach that strategically uses donor funds with a focus to scale. And which links behaviour change in communities with government leadership as well as business development and finance opportunities. So markets are developed that service base of the pyramid populations, and change sanitation behaviour for good.To this end, WASTE together with Actiam, TATA-AIG and UNU developed Financial Inclusion Improves Sanitation and Health (FINISH) in India in 2008. Due to its success and its potential scalability, the approach was replicated in Kenya (FINISH INK), where Amref Flying Doctors, representing Amref Health Africa (“Amref”), joined as partner.**FINISH aims for sanitation market development for BoP populations.** As a public private partnership it fosters stakeholders from four domains, ie communities, government, business and finance to work together on this objective. So that by the end of the day:- people know they need a toilet (through health awareness creation)- people want a toilet (through demand creation)- people want to buy a durable toilet with safe management of human waste (through sanitation marketing)- people are ready to utilise safely treated human waste from individual household toilets- local people can build those (through mason training)- people can afford those (through financial inclusion and loans, design improvements and economies of scale)- particularly in India and Bangladesh focus will be on faecal sludge management**Finish is designed to scale.** It aims to institutionalize new ways of working while unlocking economies of scale. In short it is about B’s: Base of the Pyramid, Bottom up, Behaviour Change, Business, and Brokering. As such, it has the potential to transform sanitation sectors where safely managed sanitation is yet to be introduced and where FINISH can contribute to let it become the new normal.

The present project aims to:1. Kick-start and inclusively scale the PPP for sanitation market development in 6 countries: India and Kenya (inclusive scale), Uganda, Ethiopia, Bangladesh, Tanzania (market development).2. Develop FINISH Mondial PPP with a 2030 horizon to boost scale, including a roadmap for strategic partnership building and multi-annual multi-country financing.
